## Mechanism test (code/round_substitution.py)

- at round-6 audits, round-5 report equals the record's actual value in: {'nothing moved, lying': 128, 'points moved, lying': 128}
- and never in: {'nothing moved, honest': 128, 'points moved, honest': 128}
- Qwen2.5-32B says lying at round-6 audits in the lying situations: 0.938 [0.918, 0.961] (substitution predicts ~0)
- Qwen2.5-72B says lying at round-6 audits in the lying situations: 1.000 [1.000, 1.000] (substitution predicts ~0)
- Llama-3.1-70B says lying at round-6 audits in the lying situations: 0.996 [0.988, 1.000] (substitution predicts ~0)

## Letter identity x audited round, crossed over the original and swapped files (source question, calibrated)

Cells are (round the record names) x (honest letter is the earlier or later pool letter); n=128 per cell in the honest situations.
ROUND = round-5 accuracy minus round-6, which compares worlds (each world has one checked round); LETTER = earlier-letter accuracy minus later-letter, paired within worlds.
A world and its swapped copy are the same history with the letter line flipped, so they resample together.
